content: Take ritonavir by mouth with a meal as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. It is important to take ritonavir at the same time as your other HIV protease inhibitors. Swallow the tablet form whole without crushing or chewing. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Note that the tablet and capsule forms of ritonavir may deliver different amounts of the drug. It is crucial to continue taking this medication, along with other HIV medications, exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take more or less than the prescribed dose, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval, even for a short period. Common side effects of ritonavir include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, stomach pain, dizziness, fatigue, weakness, changes in taste, or tingling/numbness around the mouth. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune system may cause symptoms, which can occur at any time during treatment, even months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking ritonavir, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas or decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet known. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking ritonavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Ritonavir may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, this medication may increase your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment with ritonavir can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor about breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Ritonavir interacts with many medications, potentially slowing down or speeding up the removal of other drugs from your body, which may affect their effectiveness. Similarly, other medications can influence how ritonavir is removed from your body, impacting its effectiveness. Examples of interacting drugs include apalutamide, rifampin, and St. John’s Wort. Ritonavir may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods (e.g., pills, patches, or rings), potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In case of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (e.g., liver function, viral load, T-cell counts, triglycerides/cholesterol, blood sugar) should be conducted. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the capsules in the refrigerator, away from light, and do not freeze them. Capsules may also be stored at room temperature if necessary, but discard them after 30 days if stored this way. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store medications in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
